description: Sentences reviewed in reading mode 2026-09-04..2026-09-18 (production, read-only). Rating by Claude, single rater, mostly from the English gloss: N natural, O forced but coherent, S word salad. Rare = effective frequency rank >5000 or unranked. Content words approximate function words by POS.

sample.arabic: اِسْتَيْقَظَ أُسَامَةُ مُتَلَهِّفًا، فَتَلَقَّطَ فِنْجَانًا وَحَقَّقَ فَحْصًا دَقِيقًا.
sample.english: Usama woke up eager, then picked up a cup and carried out a careful examination.
sample.quality_reason: The Arabic is grammatical and could plausibly occur in a simple story: Usama wakes eagerly, picks up a cup, and performs a careful inspection. The English accurately reflects the meaning.

sample.arabic: تَخْلِيصٌ سِحْرِيٌّ فِي القِصَّةِ، وَلَكِنَّ الرُّعْبَ لَمْ يَضْمَحِلَّ.
sample.english: There is a magical rescue in the story, but the terror did not fade.
sample.quality_reason: الجملة سليمة نحويًا ومفهومة، ويمكن أن تُقال بأسلوب قصصي/تعليمي: «تخليص سحري في القصة، ولكن الرعب لم يضمحل». الترجمة دقيقة لمعنى الجملة.

sample.arabic: المُتَجَوِّلُ إِسْرَائِيلِيٌّ، وَمِزَاجُهُ زَعْلانُ اللَّيْلَةَ.
sample.english: The wanderer is Israeli, and his mood is upset tonight.
sample.quality_reason: The sentence is grammatically acceptable and plausible, though slightly colloquial because of زعلان. The English accurately reflects the Arabic meaning.

sample.arabic: حَطَّ الرَّاكِبُ حِزَامَهُ عَلَى الأَرْضِ.
sample.english: The rider put down his belt on the ground.
sample.quality_reason: Grammatical and plausible; حزامه can mean his belt/strap, and the translation is accurate.

sample.arabic: اِلْتَقَيْنَا صُدْفَةً فِي المَصْرِفِ وَكَانَ لُزُومٌ أَنْ نَتَحَدَّثَ.
sample.english: We met by chance at the bank and it was necessary that we talk.
sample.quality_reason: The wording is somewhat formal and less idiomatic than كان لازمًا أن نتحدث, but it is grammatical and plausibly means there was a need for us to talk.

sample.arabic: هَلْ تَتَصَوَّرُ أَنَّ الطَّلَلَ المَهْجُورَ كَانَ صَرْحاً عَظِيماً ذَا بَهَاءٍ وَجَوْهَرٍ؟
sample.english: Do you imagine that the abandoned ruin was once a great edifice of splendor and substance?
sample.quality_reason: Grammatically sound and plausible in a literary or reflective context. The English accurately matches the Arabic meaning.

sample.arabic: لَمَعَ العَاجُ تَحْتَ سَحَرٍ رَطْبٍ، فَشَعَرَتْ حَائِرَةٌ بِغِبْطَةٍ وَعَطْفٍ.
sample.english: Ivory gleamed under a moist dawn, so a perplexed woman felt delight and compassion.
sample.quality_reason: The Arabic is grammatical and reads as literary/poetic. حائرةٌ can function substantively as 'a perplexed woman/female person,' and سَحَرٍ means dawn/pre-dawn. The English accurately reflects the meaning.

sample.arabic: أَسْدَلَ الغُلَامُ رِدَاءَهُ عَلَى كَتِفَيْهِ بِهُدُوءٍ.
sample.english: The boy lowered his cloak over his shoulders quietly.
sample.quality_reason: Grammatically correct and plausible. أسدل رداءه على كتفيه means he let down or draped his cloak over his shoulders; the English is acceptable.

sample.arabic: أَوْصَى المُصَوِّرُ بِتَجَنُّبِ الشُّحُوبِ بِالإِضَاءَةِ.
sample.english: The photographer advised avoiding pallor with lighting.
sample.quality_reason: Grammatical and plausible in a photography context, meaning the photographer advised avoiding pallor by/with lighting. The English is accurate enough.

sample.arabic: حَقيبَتُكَ مُؤَنِّبَةٌ لَكَ؛ لِأَنَّكَ تَرَكْتَ مِقْلَمَةً هُنَاكَ.
sample.english: Your bag is reproaching you, because you left a pencil case there.
sample.quality_reason: Grammatically acceptable. The bag reproaching someone is personification, but it is plausible in a story or playful context. The English matches the Arabic.

sample.arabic: طَابَ الطَّعَامُ لِلْجَمِيعِ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَضَافَتِ الخَرْدَلَ وَالبَصَلَ وَكَانَ المَذَاقُ رَائِعاً.
sample.english: The food was good for everyone after she added the mustard and onions, and the taste was wonderful.
sample.quality_reason: The Arabic is grammatical and describes a plausible situation: the food became pleasing/tasty after she added mustard and onions. The English translation accurately conveys the meaning, though 'was good for everyone' is slightly less idiomatic than 'everyone liked it.'

sample.arabic: بَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَتَغَدَّى بِالشَّوَارْمَةِ، خَطَرَ لِي سُؤَالٌ عَنِ المَعْدِنِ المُسْتَخْدَمِ فِي الشِّيشِ.
sample.english: While I was having lunch with shawarma, a question about the metal used in the skewer occurred to me.
sample.quality_reason: The Arabic is grammatically sound. The verb بَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَتَغَدَّى correctly uses the imperfect with كان to express a past continuous action. خَطَرَ لِي is a natural idiomatic construction meaning 'it occurred to me.' The prepositional phrase with المعدن is correctly constructed. The scenario (wondering about the metal skewer while eating shawarma) is plausible and coherent. The English translation accurately captures the meaning.

sample.arabic: كَفَرَ الرَّجُلُ بِالآلِهَةِ القَدِيمَةِ وَاتَّبَعَ طَرِيقاً جَدِيداً.

sample.arabic: اِعْتَدَلَ الطَّقْسُ بَعْدَ أُسْبُوعٍ مِنَ الْحَرَارَةِ الشَّدِيدَةِ وَصَارَ مُعْتَدِلًا.

sample.quality_reason: The Arabic is grammatical and plausible, though redundant because اِعْتَدَلَ and صار معتدلًا express nearly the same idea. The English accurately reflects that redundancy and meaning.
rare: اِعْتَدَلَ (to straighten up; to be moderate)

sample.arabic: اِنْتَدَبَ قَائِدٌ قَلِقٌ لِلدِّفَاعِ عَنِ السُّورِ.

sample.arabic: اِشْتَرَى الرَّجُلُ مُؤْنَةً كَثِيرَةً لِلرِّحْلَةِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مُبَالِيًا بِالتَّحْضِيرِ.

sample.arabic: المُتَصَدِّقُ وَزَّعَ عُلَبَ الطَّعَامِ وَالمَاءِ بِاسْتِعْدَادٍ كَامِلٍ.

sample.arabic: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ اِسْتِعَادَةُ الْغِبْطَةِ بَعْدَ فَقْدِ الْحَلَاوَةِ الَّتِي عَاشَتْهَا سَابِقاً؟
